text:
Olivia (Support): Escalation from AcmeCorp — they see frequent SSE disconnects on long streams, plus Python SDK iterator throws a traceback when client tries to reconnect. Customer says final partial JSON chunk is sometimes dropped and occasionally duplicated on retry. Attaching minimal logs below.

Maya (PM): Sorry to hear — any repro steps or traceback we can share here? We need to know if this is SDK or server-side. :eyes:

Olivia (Support): Pasting the traceback they captured (redacted keys):
```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "app.py", line 82, in <module>
    for chunk in client.stream_completion(...):
  File "/venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages/redwood_sdk/streaming.py", line 210, in __anext__
    raise StopAsyncIteration
StopAsyncIteration

During handling of the above exception, another exception occurred:

Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages/redwood_sdk/streaming.py", line 330, in _resume_connection
    resp = await self._handshake_resume()
  File "/venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages/httpx/_client.py", line 845, in send
    raise HTTPStatusError('401 Unauthorized')
httpx.HTTPStatusError: 401 Client Error: Unauthorized for url
```

Olivia (Support): They say token rotation happens in-process (short-lived token from internal auth service). When 401 happens mid-stream the iterator sometimes stops and raises StopAsyncIteration, or it attempts to reconnect and yields the last buffered partial chunk again, so customer sees duplicate partial JSON and sometimes an empty final frame.

Jamie (Eng): Can you include the minimal client snippet they used? Also server logs around the sequence id for that session would help.

Olivia (Support): Snippet:
```py
# simplified
async for evt in client.stream_completion(prompt, on_token=lambda t: out.append(t)):
    pass

# they rotate token in background: auth.update_token(new_token)
```
They tried calling client.close() in their auth callback before swapping token and also tried letting SDK auto-resume. Both hit trouble.

Rick (SRE): I pulled server logs for session id 8ed3a7 — I can see a reconnect at 2026-03-14T13:02:11Z with no resume_token header, and a subsequent complete stream emitted for the same logical request id at 13:02:12Z. That explains duplicate output. Also saw a 401 in-between from the edge when token refreshed mid-request.

Jamie (Eng): Ok — two things likely combined: (1) SDK resume logic doesn't atomically mark "final_frame_seen" when it drains the buffered partials, so if reconnect happens during that window we can re-emit them; (2) token-rotation path sometimes triggers a new connection without sending resume_token, causing server to treat it as fresh. Both lead to duplicate partials.

Maya (PM): Is this a regression from last week? Any customer impact billing-wise?

Olivia (Support): Customer reports extra ~15% token billing for a handful of heavy streams. They want a fix or mitigation ASAP.

Jamie (Eng): Immediate mitigation we can advise customer: before rotating token, call await client.stop_streams() (recommended helper) or set a flag to buffer-and-finish current streams. We'll add a short KB entry. For SDK fix: add an atomic state transition during reconnect that marks buffered chunks as "consumed" before attempting resume; also ensure resume_token included on reconnect path even when token rotation occurs. I'll open a PR with tests reproducing duplicate-chunk pattern.

Olivia (Support): I'll send the mitigation steps to the customer and ask them to try stop_streams() and to share results. Pls include a link to the PR once created — they want timeline. :thumbsup:

Jamie (Eng): Created a repro test locally (asyncio + simulated token expiry). Repro notes: 1) stream 60s+ with small tokens; 2) trigger auth rotate at ~30s; 3) simulate edge returning 401 on next frame; 4) then client auto-reconnects without resume_token. Observed duplicate partial chunk ~30% of runs. Logging and unit test ready.

Rick (SRE): For server hardening, I'll make the resume path more permissive: if we detect same request-id within a 5s window and the client provides client_seq_begin header, prefer resume semantics rather than treating as new. That should reduce duplicates from clients that lost resume_token during rotation. Will stage as a config toggle.

Maya (PM): Great. Can we estimate ETA for SDK patch and server toggle? Customer needs ETA to decide whether to accept mitigation or ask for immediate credit.

Jamie (Eng): I can get a small patch and release a patch SDK within 48 hours (hotfix branch). Tests + integration with token refresh flow might take that long.

Rick (SRE): I'll stage server toggle in next deploy window (8–12 hours) behind a kill-switch. If safe, roll to prod in ~12–24 hours.

Olivia (Support): I'll update AcmeCorp with two options: 1) apply client mitigation now (stop_streams() pattern) and try edge config toggle once available; 2) accept a billing credit request — I'll open billing ticket.

DeployBot: deploy queued: staging/resume-tolerance-toggle -> started

Olivia (Support): Thanks team. I'll follow up after customer tests the mitigation. Keeping thread open for PR link.

Jamie (Eng): WIP PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/1423 (adds atomic consume flag + resume_token always set on reconnect). Will update when CI passes.

Olivia (Support): CI passed and customer confirmed mitigation reduced duplicates to 0 in their smoke tests. Billing asked for only partial credit now. Closing follow-up: will monitor for any recurrence. :white_check_mark:
